hook.line: Almost every plan in Bogotá comes with a quiet condition. Instead of promising, you say it depends, and there is one small word you must not forget.

examples.en:
Are you coming tomorrow?
It depends.

examples.es: Depende de si me dan el préstamo.
examples.en: It depends on whether they give me the loan.
The price depends on the size.

rule:
*Depender* always takes *de*: *depende de* plus the thing. *De* and *el* squeeze into *del*: *depende del clima*. Before a *si* clause, it is *depende de si* (whether).

*Depende* on its own is a full answer, like English "it depends".

The verb agrees with what depends: *El precio depende*, *los precios dependen*, *dependemos de ti*.

English never lets you drop "on", and Spanish never lets you drop *de*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a verb with a fixed preposition: *depender* is always followed by *de*.

options: It will depend on the weather.
The price depends on the size.
Prices don't depend on the size.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *La respuesta ___ clima.* (*depende del* or *depende de el*) The answer depends on the weather.
Pick and type the whole sentence: *El precio ___ del tamaño.* (*depende* or *dependen*) The price depends on the size.
Say: It depends on the weather.
Say to a friend: It all depends on you.
Your friend asks if you are coming tomorrow. Answer with one word: It depends.
Make it about prices (plural): *El precio depende del tamaño.*
yourTurn.why: Plural prices need the plural verb *dependen*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It depends on whether they give me the loan.
yourTurn.answer: Depende de si me dan el préstamo.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Depender* always needs *de*, and *de* plus *el* becomes *del*.
English says depends *on*, but Spanish uses *de*, never *en*.

pitfalls.wrong: Depende si me dan el préstamo.
pitfalls.right: Depende de si me dan el préstamo.

personal: Think of a plan you have this week and give it a condition: *Voy al cine, pero depende del…* or *Depende de si…*.
